To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) component analysis is a systematic approach to ethical analysis that is useful in a variety of contexts; (b) component analysis provides a principled way of determining the ethical permissibility of research; (c) component analysis can be applied in a variety of ways, depending upon the ethical question at issue; (d) component analysis can help to resolve contemporary controversies in the ethics of research; and (e) component analysis is not a decision-making algorithm that can be applied mechanically.

(1) the ethics of clinical trials can be analyzed systematically, using a component analysis approach, (2) the ethical acceptability of a research protocol is determined by the acceptability of its components, and (3) the acceptability of each component of a protocol is determined by a risk/benefit analysis.
the ethics of research is a complex, multifactorial phenomenon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ethical evaluation of research risks.

the question of how to determine the ethical acceptability of risks to research subjects, and the development of an ethical theory of risk in research that will provide a framework for making such determinations.
the following question: When are research risks reasonable, given anticipated benefits?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risks of clinical research are reasonable in relation to the anticipated benefits of that research when the following conditions are met: The research is scientifically valid.
the risks of research must be reasonable in relation to the anticipated benefits.

“Research risks are reasonable in relation to benefits when they are no greater than the risks of standard care, and they are no greater in the research than they would have been in the absence of research, and when they are no less than the risks of the best available alternative treatment or care.”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
component analysis is a method for evaluating the ethics of risk that is both systematic and flexible enough to be used for a wide variety of research designs.
component analysis provides a systematic framework to evaluate the ethics of risk and benefit in research.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ethics of risk is a matter of balancing risks and benefits in the context of the research question, the study design, the population, the research setting and the anticipated benefits to participants.
, although it is often assumed that the risks of research must be justified by reference to anticipated benefits, the ethical justification of risks in research is actually much more complex.
the question of when research risks are reasonable in relation to benefits is not a question that can be answered in isolation.
